blockers.quote: Last year, the country grounded its planes for the English listening test. For 35 minutes, nothing takes off or lands while you listen (c02).
blockers.why: Overstated scope and narrative action stated as fact under claim c02. The 35-minute flight rescheduling specifically occurred last year (November 2025); the c02 note explicitly states that the 2026 exam plans a 25-minute window and the script must say 'last year' or use no year. Phrasing it as 'For 35 minutes, nothing takes off or lands while you listen' projects last year's duration into the present test and violates the rule that what you do in the story ('while you listen') is never stated as a cited fact.
blockers.fix: Anchor the duration and grounding strictly to last year's real-world event as supported by the c02 source quote: 'Last year, the country grounded its planes for 35 minutes during the English listening test, so no flight could take off or land (c02).'

blockers.quote: Here's what you had backwards. In most subjects, the top grade goes to the top 4 per cent of everyone in the country who sat it (c01). Not four places on a board. His grade never cost you yours.
blockers.why: The wrong belief broken by c01 is constructed as a straw man (rules/story.md #7). Setting up the misconception in lines 166–168 as believing an academy's internal poster board has only four top-grade spots ('The academy's prediction board has a hundred names. Four are marked for the top grade') describes an artificial belief no real test-taker holds. In real life, Korean students experience zero-sum competition because school-internal grades (nae-shin) were curved strictly within the school cohort (the top 4%), which students conflated with the nationwide CSAT cohort curve. By dropping c13 and reducing the misconception to 'Not four places on a board', c01 is used to knock down an absurd poster-board misunderstanding rather than the genuine zero-sum belief.
blockers.fix: Reframe the wrong belief fairly around zero-sum cohort competition rather than an academy poster: 'Here's what you had backwards. In most subjects, the top grade goes to the top 4 per cent of everyone in the country who sat it (c01). Your classmates' scores never took yours away. His grade never cost you yours.'
